method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; four regulative rules (s 13 (2) answer within 2 weeks; s 13B (2) / s 13BA (2) access by the 30-day or fee day; s 16B (2) record to the nominated provider within 2 weeks; principles 12.1 and 12.2 copy to the new provider) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Health Records (Privacy and Access) Act 1997 (ACT), A1997-125, Republication No 32 (R32), effective 16 November 2025, last amended by A2025-29, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/A1997-125.txt
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is (c) Australian Capital Territory, used under CC BY 4.0; see SOURCE-LICENSE.md
seat: the consumer: the individual whose health record it is (or who used the health service), and those the Act lets act for one (a person with parental responsibility, a guardian, the legal representative or, if none, an immediate family member of a consumer who has died); typically the patient getting their records before a medical negligence or injury claim, or the injured person whose insurer or employer wants a medical report (hrpa-consumer.l4)
focus: the ACT's health records and health complaints law, taken as the equivalent of the health records Acts named for other jurisdictions: access to one's own health record and its deadlines, deemed refusal and complaint, health status reports (insurers' and employers' medical reports), consent to disclosure, keeping and destruction, transfer to a new provider

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run hrpa-dates.l4 ; l4 run hrpa-consumer.l4 ; l4 run hrpa-cases.l4
checks.result: 197 assertions written, 197 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07, after the verification fixes); a deliberately wrong assertion in a scratch copy showed as failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: s 7; Part 3 (not whole) ss 9, 10 (1)-(3), (7), (8), 10A, 12, 13 (with (5)), 13A, 13B, 13BA (2), (6), 13C, 13D, 14, 14A, 15, 16A, 16B, 16D, 17; s 18; ss 20-23 (maximum penalties); ss 25-27 (with the void consents of ss 26 (2), 27 (3)); ss 31, 32; schedule 1 principles 4.1 cl 2-3, 6 cl 4, 7 cl 3, 10 cl 2 (c) and cl 7, 11 cl 2, 3 (b), 5, 6, 12.1 and 12.2 cl 2-4. Out: ss 1-6, 8, 10 (4)-(6), 11, 13BA (3)-(5), 16, 16C, 24, 29, 30, 33, 34, 36, 37, the offence elements, and the other privacy principle clauses (duties with no deadline or turning on reasonableness; their breach is asked as a fact for s 18). Reasons in NOTES.md.
